statusDetail: Coverage-complete multi-template audit of public, unauthenticated paths. Authenticated purchasing, seller dashboards, chat, payment execution, and post-login account management were not covered because they require an account and real transaction; representative public entry points were covered instead.

paths.description: Marketplace entry and game-discovery index; represents global navigation, search, consent, localization, and the unusually long catalog page.
Representative marketplace category/listing and the start of the purchase journey, including filters, seller rows, prices, and sale action.
Authentication path, including third-party identity, password entry, CAPTCHA, mobile reflow, focus, and motion preference.
Account creation form used to inspect labels, autofill, validation, consent, CAPTCHA, and recovery behavior.
Long-form policy/content archetype used to inspect headings, legibility, localization, and responsive document layout.
Representative HTTP failure route used to inspect error-state recovery.

findings.summary: The interface ignores the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode capture is visually identical to the light capture; the computed body remains white and the CSS probe found no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark design tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Reduced-motion is not explicitly respected.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, login controls and the cookie modal retain 150–300 ms transitions; the CSS probe found no reduced-motion query.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce rule that removes non-essential modal and control transitions.

findings.summary: Page and state changes are abrupt rather than continuity-preserving.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe across all five templates found no view-transition declarations, while the marketplace uses cross-document navigation between index, listing, and account pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation, with a no-motion path for reduced-motion users.

findings.summary: The 47,777 px catalog provides no scroll-reactive orientation aid.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout measured a 47,777 px document; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, scroll timeline, or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a compact sticky catalog index or progress/orientation aid that responds to scroll state.

findings.summary: Alphabet jumps do not visibly cue the destination.
findings.evidence: The homepage exposes A–Z hash links, but the probe found no target highlight or transition and screenshots show only a static index.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a brief, reduced-motion-safe :target highlight and preserve focus when jumping to a catalog section.

findings.summary: The cookie banner obscures core content on every first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop captures show a fixed banner covering listing rows and page footer; on 360 px mobile it occupies roughly the bottom 29% of the viewport and blocks catalog content.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the persistent blocking banner with a compact, immediately actionable consent surface that includes equally visible accept/reject controls.

findings.summary: Consent preferences use custom dialog semantics instead of the native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The DOM reports a DIV with role=dialog, but zero dialog, popover, or details elements across templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal consent preferences and native close/cancel behavior, with focus containment and restoration.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The same marketplace controls are reused across index, listing, and forms, but CSS inspection found no @container or container-type declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable search, filter, and account-card components where their available inline size changes.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and target sizing are unreliable.
findings.evidence: The active focus probe found outline:none on the navigation toggle, search field, and icon-only submit button; Lighthouse also failed target-size, and the toggle measured only 26×34 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear :focus-visible styling and ensure interactive targets are at least 44×44 CSS px or have equivalent spacing.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a clear page-level purpose and overwhelms discovery.
findings.evidence: The first template has no H1 or main landmark and contains 4,953 links in a 47,777 px alphabetical catalog; the first viewport competes with a large promotion and consent banner.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a clear H1 and concise marketplace purpose, prioritize search and popular categories, and progressively reveal the full alphabetic catalog.

findings.summary: Registration validation provides no inspectable invalid state before CAPTCHA submission.
findings.evidence: An empty registration submit reported form.checkValidity() true, no :invalid controls, and no role=alert/error output; name, email, and password inputs omit required constraints.
findings.suggestedFix: Add client-side semantic constraints and accessible, field-linked error summaries while retaining server validation and CAPTCHA.

findings.summary: Mobile lab LCP is outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.9 s, FCP 2.6 s, and Speed Index 4.8 s (performance 0.75), although the desktop trace was faster at LCP 1.02 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP resource and remove critical-path blocking so mobile LCP is consistently below 2.5 s.

findings.summary: A synchronous head script and stylesheet delay rendering.
findings.evidence: HAR identified main.css and app.bundle.js as render-blocking candidates; DOM confirmation shows app.bundle.js is in <head> with neither async nor defer. Lighthouse estimates 1,450 ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer the application bundle, inline only critical CSS, and load remaining styles without blocking first render.

findings.summary: The initial payload contains substantial unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 49 KiB unused CSS and 44 KiB unused JavaScript on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Split template-specific code and remove unused framework/icon styles from the critical bundle.

findings.summary: Core controls and fields lack accessible names or persistent labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name and link-name; probes show zero labels on search, login, email, and password inputs, plus two homepage images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible <label> elements, accessible names for icon-only controls, and appropriate alt text or empty alt for decorative images.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed on the representative homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust muted text and control colors to meet WCAG AA contrast in every theme and state.

findings.summary: Landmark and focus structure is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found no main landmark; the homepage has no H1, and focus probes show outline:none on several primary controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in <main>, restore a logical H1 hierarchy, and provide consistent :focus-visible indicators.

findings.summary: Small interactive targets reduce touch and zoom usability.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed target-size; the focus probe measured the menu toggle at 26×34 px and the search submit at 24×38 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes and spacing to at least 44×44 CSS px while preserving the successful narrow-viewport reflow.

findings.summary: Images are not dimensioned and one key raster asset is not responsive.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all three images missing explicit dimensions; the 1600 px JPEG lacks srcset, and Lighthouse failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio and responsive srcset/sizes; preserve intrinsic aspect ratios.

findings.summary: Some controls masquerade as links and are not crawlable.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found three javascript: links and Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for in-page actions and real href URLs for navigable destinations.

findings.summary: The advertised sitemap endpoint returns an HTML 404.
findings.evidence: A direct request to /sitemap.xml returned the site’s “page not found” HTML; canonical and hreflang are otherwise present on core pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt; keep localized canonicals and hreflang consistent.

findings.summary: Public pages lack social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: Probes found valid JSON-LD on homepage/listing but no Open Graph metadata on any representative template.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph and Twitter Card metadata for marketplace and listing pages.

findings.summary: Key browser security headers are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. HTTPS, HSTS, and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; retain HSTS and frame protection.

findings.summary: Authentication offers passwords and federated providers but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login UI exposes Google, VK, username/email, password, and CAPTCHA; probes found no WebAuthn/passkey affordance. No permission prompt appeared on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration, authentication, recovery, and reauthentication alongside existing methods.

findings.summary: Defense-in-depth policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff are absent, even though clickjacking protection and HSTS are configured.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, strict referrer controls, and a minimal Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for account surfaces.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually asymmetric.
findings.evidence: The banner presents a prominent blue “Agree to all” action while the neutral “Options” path is secondary and no equally visible reject action appears; it blocks content on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent accept, reject, and customize actions with neutral copy and preserve service without non-essential consent.

findings.summary: Registration lacks semantic, accessible pre-submit validation.
findings.evidence: The empty registration form is considered valid by the browser, exposes no required constraints, aria-invalid state, or live error summary, and is gated by CAPTCHA.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required/type/autocomplete attributes, validate after interaction, and announce a concise linked error summary.

findings.summary: Authentication and signup fields omit standard autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: Login username/password autocomplete values are empty; signup email is empty and signup password explicitly uses autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use username, current-password, email, new-password, and name autocomplete tokens as appropriate.

findings.summary: The hero artwork is not responsively or format optimized.
findings.evidence: The image audit found a 1600 px, 247.8 KiB JPEG without srcset or dimensions; Lighthouse estimates 227 KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes, explicit dimensions, and a size matched to the rendered slot.
